question: How many tonnes of pizza do people in Chicago eat on an average day in 2026?

target.what: Total mass of pizza consumed by people in Chicago (city of Chicago, Illinois) on a single average day in calendar year 2026, counting all pizza eaten by residents and visitors within the city, expressed as metric tons per day
target.cadence: Single annual average daily flow, no official series
target.caveats: Ambiguous scope: 'people in Chicago' could mean residents only (population ~2.7M) or all persons present including commuters and tourists (~3.5-4M daytime/visitor-adjusted). Working interpretation: all pizza consumed within Chicago city limits on an average day, by residents plus visitors/commuters

candidates.hypothesis: National or Chicago-metro pizza restaurant sales (USD) divided by average price per pizza and average pizza weight gives tonnes; target = (Chicago pizza sales USD/day) / (USD per pizza) * (kg per pizza) / 1000. Sales scale with population and income; Chicago share of US pizza sales approximates its share of population or food spending.
candidates.data_to_find: US pizza restaurant industry annual sales (e.g., PMQ Pizza Magazine, IBISWorld, Technomic) for 2024-2025; Chicago metro or city pizza sales if available; average price per pizza and average pizza weight (ounces) from industry surveys or chain menu data. Minimum: national sales, Chicago population share, price per pie, weight per pie.
search_hints: US pizza industry annual sales 2024 billion
average price of a pizza 2025
Chicago pizza market size restaurants

candidates.hypothesis: Per-capita pizza consumption frequency (pizza eating occasions per person per week) times average grams per occasion times population gives daily mass. Target = population * occasions/person/day * g/occasion / 1e6. US dietary surveys (NHANES) give pizza intake grams and frequency; Chicago population from Census.
candidates.data_to_find: NHANES or USDA data on mean pizza intake (grams per eating occasion) and percent of population eating pizza on a given day; pizza eating frequency per week; Chicago population 2025-2026 estimate. Substitute: national per-capita pizza consumption (lb/year) from USDA/industry.

Target = (N stores * pies/store/day * kg/pie) + retail pizza mass. Store counts from business listings; throughput from operator benchmarks.
candidates.data_to_find: Count of pizza restaurants in Chicago (Yelp/Google/Census County Business Patterns NAICS 722513), average daily pizza sales per pizzeria (industry benchmarks, POS data), average pizza weight. Minimum: store count and per-store daily pie volume.

methods.label: m1

p18.role: Chicago resident population in 2025, used as the 2026 resident base

a2.role: pizza eating occasions per person per day in Chicago, 2026

a1.role: mean grams of pizza per eating occasion, 2026

methods.rationale: Base-rate route: resident population times daily pizza occasion rate times grams per occasion. Uses NHANES prevalence and CSFII grams as anchors via assumptions a1/a2. Covers residents only; visitors are handled in m3. Main failure modes: occasion rate and grams per occasion are both uncertain and correlated with Chicago's pizza culture.
methods.error: covers only residents of population, so code does not combine it with full estimates; sum it with its siblings (visitors) in one method, with an allowance assumption for parts without evidence

methods.label: m2

p22.role: count of pizza restaurants in Chicago, April 2026

a4.role: realised pizzas sold per Chicago pizzeria per day, 2026

a3.role: average pizza mass per pie, kg

a5.role: share of Chicago pizza mass from non-restaurant channels

methods.rationale: Capacity/throughput route: Chicago pizzeria count times realised pies per store per day times pie mass, grossed up for non-restaurant channels. The 1,987 count is a listing artifact and the 100/day benchmark is generic, so a4 is deliberately below it. Main failure modes: store count overstates active venues; pie weight and channel share are uncertain.

methods.label: m3

params.formula: (p18 + p59 * a6 / k_days_per_year) * a2 * a1 + (p59 * a6 / k_days_per_year) * a2 * a7 * a1

p18.role: Chicago resident population in 2025, used as the 2026 resident base

a2.role: pizza eating occasions per person per day in Chicago, 2026

a1.role: mean grams of pizza per eating occasion, 2026

a7.role: visitor pizza occasion rate relative to residents

methods.rationale: Exposure route: resident person-days plus visitor person-days (visits times stay length divided by days per year) times pizza occasion rate and grams per occasion, with visitors at a higher relative rate. Converts visits to person-days via a6. Main failure modes: visitor stay length and relative rate are assumptions; commuters are not separately counted and are absorbed into the resident base.

methods.label: m4

params.formula: (p18 + p59 * a6 / k_days_per_year * a10) * a8 * a9

p18.role: Chicago resident population in 2025, used as the 2026 resident base

a10.role: visitor pizza rate relative to residents in the per-capita benchmark route

a8.role: US per-capita pizza mass per person per day, 2026

a9.role: Chicago pizza-affinity multiplier relative to US average

methods.rationale: Per-capita benchmark route summed over residents and visitors: US per-capita pizza mass (anchored on AGMRC per-capita spend p160 and pie mass) times Chicago population times a modest Chicago affinity multiplier, plus visitor person-days weighted by a10. Main failure modes: per-capita mass is derived from spend and price assumptions; affinity multiplier is weakly evidenced; visitor weighting is unc

kept.name: Mean grams of pizza per eating occasion, all ages, 2026
kept.rationale: CSFII 1994-96 gives 169 g/occasion (p123) and 175 g/consumer-day (p130); NHANES 2007-2010 energy data (744 kcal adult, 538 kcal child, 220-370 kcal/slice, p145-p148) imply roughly 2-3 slices, i.e. 200-350 g. Central 200 g with wide range bridges old gram data and energy data to 2026.
kept.applies_when: Used to convert pizza eating occasions into mass for people present in Chicago in 2026.
kept.falsified_by: A current NHANES/WWEIA estimate of grams per pizza occasion materially outside 140-290 g.

kept.name: Pizza eating occasions per person per day, Chicago 2026
kept.rationale: NHANES any-day prevalence of 11% (p10/p111) with some consumers eating pizza more than once, the 1986 Chicago frequency of 34.8 meals/yr (p56, ~0.095/day), and the 2025 survey showing 35% eating pizza more than weekly (p105). Central 0.16/day (~58/yr) reflects Chicago's above-average pizza culture a
kept.applies_when: Used as the per-person daily pizza occasion rate for people present in Chicago in 2026.
kept.falsified_by: A current Chicago-specific dietary survey showing occasion rates outside 0.10-0.24 per person per day.

kept.name: Average pizza mass per pie (restaurant and retail)
kept.rationale: A medium 8-slice pizza at 220-370 kcal/slice (p147/p148) and ~250-280 kcal/100 g implies roughly 0.7-1.2 kg; deep-dish Chicago pies are heavier. Central 1.0 kg with wide range.
kept.applies_when: Used to convert pizza counts into mass in the capacity route.
kept.falsified_by: A measured average Chicago pie weight outside 0.7-1.4 kg.

kept.name: Realised pizzas sold per Chicago pizzeria per day, 2026
kept.rationale: The generic 100/day benchmark (p37) is a national chain-style figure; the 1,987 listing count (p22) includes many small and marginal venues, so realised throughput per listed venue is lower. Central 60 with wide range.
kept.applies_when: Used with the Chicago pizzeria count to estimate restaurant pizza mass.
kept.falsified_by: Chicago-specific POS or health-inspection throughput data showing materially different per-store volumes.

kept.name: Share of Chicago pizza mass from non-restaurant channels (retail frozen, convenience, other)
kept.rationale: USDA reports 59% of pizza consumption at home (p152) and 6% from 'other' sources (p16); restaurant pizza is the majority but retail/frozen and other channels are material. Central 25% with wide range.
kept.applies_when: Used to gross up restaurant pizza mass to all pizza eaten in Chicago.
kept.falsified_by: Chicago-specific channel data showing non-restaurant share outside 15-40%.

kept.name: Average visitor-days per Chicago visitor, 2026
kept.rationale: 56.8M annual visitors (p59) are visits, not unique persons; typical city leisure/business trips average roughly 2 days. Needed to convert visits into person-days of exposure.
kept.applies_when: Used to add visitor person-days to resident person-days in the exposure route.
kept.falsified_by: Choose Chicago stay-length data showing average stays outside 1.4-3.0 days.

kept.name: Visitor pizza occasion rate relative to residents
kept.rationale: Visitors eat out more and Chicago pizza is a tourist draw, but they also have fewer total eating occasions in the city. Central 1.2x resident rate with wide range.
kept.applies_when: Used to scale visitor person-days into pizza occasions.
kept.falsified_by: Visitor dietary or spending data showing visitor pizza rates outside 0.8-1.8x resident rates.

kept.name: Average pizza mass per person per day, US benchmark 2026
kept.rationale: US per-capita pizza restaurant spend of ~$213/yr (p160) at ~$15-20 per pizza and ~1 kg per pizza implies roughly 10-14 kg/yr, i.e. ~0.03 kg/day restaurant pizza; adding retail raises it. Central 0.030 kg/day with wide range.
kept.applies_when: Used as a per-capita benchmark scaled to Chicago's population and pizza affinity.
kept.falsified_by: US per-capita pizza mass estimates outside 0.018-0.050 kg/day.

kept.name: Chicago pizza-affinity multiplier relative to US average
kept.rationale: Chicago was ranked the top US pizza city in 1986 (p56) and has a strong deep-dish/taproom culture; a modest above-average multiplier is plausible. Central 1.15 with wide range.
kept.applies_when: Used to adjust the US per-capita pizza mass benchmark to Chicago.
kept.falsified_by: Chicago-specific consumption data showing per-capita pizza mass at or below the US average.

kept.name: Visitor share of Chicago pizza mass relative to their person-day share
kept.rationale: Allows the visitor component of the per-capita benchmark route to be scaled up or down relative to residents; central 1.0 means visitors eat pizza at the same per-person-day rate as residents, with wide uncertainty. Needed because m4 must sum residents and visitors in one method.
kept.applies_when: Used in the summed per-capita benchmark route to weight visitor person-days.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that visitors' pizza rate differs materially from residents' beyond 0.6-1.6x.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
